claims.text: A WVTaTiCr refractory high-entropy-alloy coating can be prepared on 42-CrMo steel by laser cladding.
The initial WVTaTiCr coating has a disordered BCC matrix.
The WVTaTiCr coating has the potential to precipitate secondary phases.
Sliding-wear behavior should be tested in air over temperatures ranging from room temperature to 1000 °C.
Wear resistance will initially improve as ambient temperature rises to approximately 600–700 °C.
Formation of a dense protective oxide scale at moderate temperature will reduce wear.
Elevated temperature can produce a transition from dislocation glide to diffusion-controlled dislocation climb or creep in high-entropy alloys.
Dislocation climb will enhance coating ductility and reduce abrasive wear.
The relevant oxide-scale transition is from a protective Cr-rich scale to non-protective Mn-rich or W-rich oxides.
Brittle C14 Laves phases can increase cracking tendency when embedded in a BCC-based high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Once the WVTaTiCr BCC matrix exceeds its stability limit, Laves phases will nucleate or coarsen.
Laves phases in the coating will act as crack-initiation sites and cause embrittlement.
A porous or non-adherent oxide scale will lose its protective function and accelerate oxidative wear.
Wear rate will follow a non-monotonic curve, decreasing initially and then increasing sharply above approximately 700–800 °C.
Performance will degrade significantly above approximately 800 °C or when the oxide scale becomes porous and non-adherent.
Oxidation of a Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloy increases substantially between 900 and 1100 °C.
A critical degradation range of 800–1000 °C is suggested for the WVTaTiCr coating by trends transferred from other alloy systems.
Specific wear rate, oxide-scale properties, Laves-phase fraction, roughness, and crack density can be measured after temperature-controlled pin-on-disk tests.

contradictions.description: The proposed degradation boundary shifts among a critical threshold of about 600–700 °C, a sharp wear-rate increase above 700–800 °C, significant degradation above 800 °C, and an uncertain critical range of 800–1000 °C.

The intervention and baseline specify room-temperature testing, but the listed experiment begins at 300 °C. This omits the stated room-temperature control needed to evaluate immediate deterioration from room temperature.

The mechanism acknowledges that Laves phases may form or dissolve depending on temperature, yet it specifically predicts nucleation or coarsening above the BCC stability limit without defining why the dissolution trend reported in the cited CrMoNbWV system would not apply.
